Quick actions

Everything stays on this phone. Back up regularly from Records.
How to measure
  1. Load a PDF farm map (or a photo of the sheet) in Maps.
  2. On Measure, tap two points a known distance apart, enter the distance in metres and calibrate.
  3. Tap points to measure a distance, or trace a boundary to get the area in hectares.
  4. Save the measurement to keep it with your field records.

Checks this phone and the app. Send a screenshot of the result if something fails.

PSC Field Maps guide

 

  
Everything the app can do, and how to use it. Your maps, notes and records stay on your own phone. Sharing between people is done by sending files.

  
What the app can do
    
   
  • Open very large PDF farm maps (hundreds of MB) and keep them sharp when you zoom in.
    • 
   
  • Work offline once a map is prepared. The last map reopens by itself.
    • 
   
  • Measure distance and area, with your choice of units.
    • 
   
  • Show your GPS position on georeferenced maps, centred as you move, with your own pointer style.
    • 
   
  • Show your travel speed and the time left to your destination.
    • 
   
  • Plan routes, save them, compare them and follow them with spoken guidance.
    • 
   
  • Find a road route from A to B on the farm road network, with warnings for open and conservation areas, rerouting when a road is missed, and arrival time from your average speed.
    • 
   
  • Mark hazards (closed gates, damaged roads) and spot-view photos.
    • 
   
  • Drop pins that become field notes with photos, video and voice.
    • 
   
  • Record walked or driven tracks, either a distance or an area, and share them as GPX or KML.
    • 
   
  • Rotate the map with two fingers, and use full screen.
    • 
  

  
Video: plan and follow a route
   
A 30-second demonstration: plan a route by tapping points, save it, tap Follow and drive it with the map following you.

   

   
Tip: the video plays from this phone, no data needed. Voice guidance has no sound in the demo; turn Voice on in the app to hear it.

  

  
1. Add and prepare a map
   
   
Open Maps, tap Add PDF maps and pick your file. Tap Prepare sharp tiles (one time). Preparing can take a while for a big map, so keep the screen on. After that the map opens quickly, works without signal and stays sharp at deep zoom.

   
Each prepared map shows a sharpness tag. If a map looks soft when you zoom in, prepare it again in this version.

  

  
2. Move around the map
   
    
   
  • Drag with one finger to pan. Pinch to zoom.
    • 
   
  • Twist with two fingers to rotate. The arrow shows north. Tap Rotate for a quarter turn.
    • 
   
  • Full gives the whole screen to the map. Tap Exit to come back.
    • 
   
  • Fit shows the whole map again.
    • 
  

  
3. Measure distance and area
   
    
   
  • Tap Measure. The measuring menu opens: Length, Area, Undo, Clear.
    • 
   
  • Tap points on the map. The reading bar at the top shows the result, with your chosen units and the other unit as well.
    • 
   
  • Tap Save in the reading bar to keep it in Records.
    • 
   
  • Tap Measure again to close the menu. While it is closed, taps do not add points.
    • 
   
  • Units: use the buttons in the reading bar. Distance can be Auto, m or km. Area can be Auto, m² or ha.
    • 
  

  
4. GPS on the map
   
    
   
  • Tap ◎ Me. Allow location when the phone asks. The map keeps your position in the centre as you move.
    • 
   
  • If you drag the map away, the button changes to Re-centre. Tap it to lock on again.
    • 
   
  • The small ring shows how accurate the fix is. In poor signal, move to open sky.
    • 
   
  • Your speed shows at the bottom left of the map.
    • 
   
  • Pointer: choose Dot, Arrow, Car, Bakkie, Walker or Pin on the GPS tab, or tap GPS tools then Pointer on the map. Car, Bakkie, Arrow and Walker turn to face your direction of travel.
    • 
  

  
5. If your position is wrong
   
    
   
  • Tap GPS tools on the map. Then use Map flip to try each orientation until the dot moves the right way when you travel. This fixes maps whose location data is flipped. The choice is remembered for that map.
    • 
   
  • Use Fix position to correct a small constant shift. Stand at a known spot, tap Fix position, then tap that spot on the map. Reset fix removes it.
    • 
   
  • Phone location must be allowed for Chrome. Turn on precise location in the phone settings.
    • 
  

  
6. Plan and follow a route
   
Watch the video topic above for the full walk-through.
    
   
  • Tap Route. Tap points along your planned route. Use Undo, Move point, Delete point or Reverse to adjust.
    • 
   
  • The panel shows distance and an estimated time. Compare saved routes in the Library.
    • 
   
  • Save the route with a name. Tick Main route for routes you use often. They show on the map automatically.
    • 
   
  • Tap Follow to navigate. The map follows you and shows distance left, time left at your actual speed, and the next point.
    • 
   
  • Before it starts, a Start navigation window lets you confirm voice on or off, head up or north up, and what to do if you leave the route (see section 7, Road navigation).
    • 
   
  • The arrival time uses the average speed you have actually driven, not a fixed guess.
    • 
   
  • Heading up turns the map so the way you travel is at the top.
    • 
   
  • Voice on/off controls spoken guidance: turns, off-route, hazards ahead, halfway and arrival. Keep the screen awake and the volume up.
    • 
   
  • Use part of a saved route by choosing a start and end point in the Library.
    • 
  

  
7. Road navigation (A to B)
    
   
  • One-time set-up for each map: go to Maps, open the map and scan it. The scan reads the Road layer and the green and grey open-area shapes, then builds the road network and saves it with the map. Big maps can take a few minutes. Keep the screen on and close other apps. Scan one map at a time.
    • 
   
  • If a map was scanned in an older version, scan it again to get the latest road types and fixes.
    • 
   
  • Navigate: tap Navigate on the map. Step 1: where are you? Use My position or Tap on map. Step 2: where are you going? Use Find compartment or Tap on map. Clear starts again.
    • 
   
  • Road priority: tar (yellow) is preferred, then plantation main road (thick dotted), then compartment road (brown dotted). Dead ends (red dotted) are avoided. The blue route is the best one. A green route appears only when it is clearly shorter and uses more compartment roads.
    • 
   
  • Tap Use as route to load a route into the planner, or Follow now to start navigating.
    • 
   
  • Open and conservation areas: if the route passes through green or grey open areas, an orange warning box lists each crossing with its length. Orange numbers mark them on the route. Tap Avoid on one section, or Avoid all for the whole trip. The app then looks for a way around.
    • 
   
  • Show road network on the map draws every road the app knows. Amber is tar, blue is plantation main road, pink is compartment road, grey is minor track, red is dead end, cyan is a link the app added. Use it to check why a route looks wrong. Pink roads should only lie on the farms you can see.
    • 
   
  • Mark blocked road: tap the map where a road is blocked or does not exist, for example a stream crossing. The spot shows a red cross and routes avoid it. Tap the cross again to remove it. Clear blocked roads removes them all for that map.
    • 
   
  • Farm to farm: if no mapped road joins two farms, the route follows roads to the edge of the first farm, then shows a dashed straight line to the next farm. A warning tells you how many km are unmapped. Follow the real public road there and watch for turns. The same applies if you start between farms.
    • 
   
  • Start navigation window: opens every time you tap Follow. Voice guidance: On or Off. Map direction: Head up or North up. If I leave the route: Ask me first, Reroute automatically or Do nothing. Your choices are remembered. Tap Start to begin or Cancel.
    • 
   
  • Missed a road: if you leave the route, a red row appears: Reroute from here or Keep going. Keep going silences it for 2 minutes. With automatic reroute the app finds a new way by itself, at most once a minute.
    • 
   
  • While following, Reroute in the bar gives two choices: Road blocked ahead marks the road about 35 m ahead as blocked and finds another way from your position, or Recalculate reroutes without blocking anything.
    • 
   
  • Voice: turns, off-route, hazards ahead, halfway and arrival. For open areas it says a warning before you start, again about 250 m before one ("Open area ahead"), when you enter it and when you leave it.
    • 
   
  • Arrival time: shows the clock time you will arrive and the time left. Until you have driven about 300 m it uses your saved speed. After that it uses your real average speed while moving. Stops do not lower it.
    • 
   
  • If a route looks wrong: the map may need a rescan, or a road may be missing from the drawing. Turn on the road network view and compare it with the map. A start that is far from any road means no mapped road is near you.
    • 
   
  • The road network is a guide. Always check gates, bridges and closed roads on the ground.
    • 
  

  
8. Hazards and spot views
   
    
   
  • Tap Spots. Add a hazard such as a closed gate, damaged road, bridge problem, fallen tree or washout, either at your position or on the map.
    • 
   
  • Mark each as Permanent or Temporary until fixed. When it is repaired, mark it Fixed.
    • 
   
  • Spot view is a photo of an important place with the date it was last updated, like a street view for the farm.
    • 
   
  • Share spots and hazards with colleagues using Export file to share. They open the file with Import file and the records merge.
    • 
  

  
9. Pins and notes
   
    
   
  • Tap Pin, then tap the map where you want the pin. Add a title, a note and a photo, then Save pin. You can also use Drop at my position.
    • 
   
  • Every pin is a field note with its location. It appears in your Notes library and on the map.
    • 
   
  • Tap a pin on the map to read it, change it or delete it. Open in Notes takes you to the full note.
    • 
   
  • On the Notes tab you can write notes with photos, video and voice, and export a note as a card with a map picture of the area.
    • 
  

  
10. Record a track
    
   
  • On the map, tap Track in the menu. Choose Distance or Area, then Start. You can record without leaving the map. (The GPS tab has the same controls plus sharing.)
    • 
   
  • For an area, walk or drive around the edge. The area and perimeter update as you go.
    • 
   
  • Press Start, then Stop at the end. Name it, check the date and time, and tap Save.
    • 
   
  • Share GPX or Share KML sends the file through your phone's share menu. Saved tracks also have Rename / date and Share in Records.
    • 
   
  • Keep the screen on while tracking.
    • 
  

  
11. Sharing and backups
    
   
  • Share the app with Share app. Each person keeps their own data on their own phone.
    • 
   
  • Share tracks, routes, spots and notes by file. Nothing is sent to a server.
    • 
   
  • Keep a backup of your records from the Records tab.
    • 
  

  
12. Updates and offline
    
   
  • When an update is ready a bar appears at the bottom. Tap Reload. Your saved maps and records stay.
    • 
   
  • Install the app from Chrome's menu with Add to Home screen. It then opens like a normal app and works offline.
    • 
   
  • The version number is shown at the bottom of the Home page.
    • 
  

  
Tips
    
   
  • Keep the screen on and the phone charged for long tracks and navigation.
    • 
   
  • The map's sharpness never drops to save memory. If the phone struggles, close other apps.
    • 
   
  • Maps without location data can still be measured after you set a known distance on the Measure tab, but they cannot show GPS.
    •
